subject: [PATCH v6 12/12] selftests/mm: add PMD swap entry tests

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch adds a set of tests to the Linux kernel's selftest suite to exercise the PMD swap entry paths. The tests cover various scenarios, including faulting in swapped pages, handling userfaultfd RWP, and verifying that VmSwap accounting is correct. The tests also check for proper behavior when unmapping or remapping pages, as well as when using zswap without PTE fallback. The patch adds a new test program, pmd_swap.c, which contains the test code, and updates the Makefile and run_vmtests.sh to include the new test.

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary: The reviewer questioned how the patch ensures that the PMD swap entry is on the specified device (PMD_SWAP_DEVICE), noting that MADV_PAGEOUT may place it on a higher-priority active swap device, which could cause the test to pass with zswap enabled and fail with it disabled. The reviewer suggested requiring PMD_SWAP_DEVICE to be the only active swap device.
reviews.raw_body:
How do we know the PMD swap entry is on PMD_SWAP_DEVICE?

Assume another higher-priority swap device is active. MADV_PAGEOUT may
place the entry there, so swapoff() operates on the wrong device. This
can make the test pass with zswap enabled and fail with it disabled.

Should PMD_SWAP_DEVICE be required to be the only active swap device?

Cheers, Lance

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a potential issue with the swapoff test not being exercised always due to the PMD_SWAP_DEVICE check, agreed to restructure the swapoff test in v2 so that it runs only when PMD_SWAP_DEVICE identifies the sole active swap device.
reviews.raw_body:
Ah yeah, you are right. I dont like it as it will likely mean that the
swapoff test wont be exercised always, but I will change the swapoff
test so that it now runs only when PMD_SWAP_DEVICE identifies the sole
active swap device, ensuring pageout and swapoff target the same backend.

2026-08-19.patch_summary: This patch adds a series of tests to the Linux kernel's selftest suite to exercise the PMD swap entry paths. The tests cover various scenarios, including faulting in swapped pages, handling of shared swap entries between parent and child processes, and interactions with userfaultfd (UFFD) and zswap. The tests also verify correct behavior for operations such as munmap, mprotect, split_munmap, uffdio_move, mremap, pagemap, mincore, madvise_free, madvise_willneed, and swapoff. The patch includes a new test program (pmd_swap.c) and updates the Makefile to include it in the selftest suite.

reviews.author: Luiz Capitulino
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Luiz Capitulino noted that do_huge_pmd_swap_page() in the swap-in path does not exercise the swapin_sync() code path, and suggested a workaround involving running the test from a cgroup and triggering reclaim manually. Additionally, he questioned whether the code was generated by AI and requested an Assisted-by tag if so.

The reviewer suggested that the swapoff test should be self-contained within its own test file instead of being part of the fixture, which is responsible for teardown.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for addressing the comments against v5, here's two general
comments:

1. On looking a bit closer at this, I realized that during swap-in
do_huge_pmd_swap_page() is retrieving the folio from the swap cache
and not exercising the swapin_sync() code path (at least this is the case
on a KVM a guest). I was able to workaround this on a test app by running
it from a cgroup and triggering reclaim manually after swap-out but before
swap-in. I'm not sure how complex it would be for you to implement this though

2. Did you use AI to generate this code? If yes, please add the
Assisted-by tag. I'm saying this because the code is weirdly uniform
and there's a bit of uneeded complexity

Small nits below, but the parts that I reviewed look good to me.

---

This seeems to be specific to the swapoff test? If yes, it would be
better to have it contained in the test itself not the fixture.
